title: Crude Venom from Sea Anemone Macrodactyla doreensis Suppresses Glioblastoma via the p53 Pathway.
authors: Lin, Limin; Huang, Meiling; Yang, Wanting; Hua, Ziqiang; Chen, Zhen; He, Panmin; Mao, Kailin; Cheng, Shuanghuai; Ma, Linlin; Cui, Shuaiying; Yi, Bo; Gao, Bingmiao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究海葵粗毒通过p53通路抑制胶质母细胞瘤，虽含AlphaFold2结构建模与分子对接，但核心是毒液抗癌药理学，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Glioblastoma is a highly invasive primary brain tumor with a poor prognosis, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Toxins derived from Macrodactyla doreensis have attracted attention for their potential anticancer activity. This study evaluated the anticancer and cytotoxic effects of M. doreensis crude venom on two commonly used glioblastoma cell lines (U251 and LN229), which mirror the phenotype of primary tumors. Cell viability and proliferation were assessed using the CCK-8 assay and colony formation assay, while cell migration and invasion capabilities were detected via wound healing assay and Transwell assay. Annexin V/PI staining and PI-based cell cycle analysis indicated that the crude venom significantly induced cell apoptosis and caused S-phase arrest. Proteomic analysis combined with GO and KEGG enrichment analyses as well as bioinformatics approaches showed that M. doreensis crude venom inhibits glioblastoma cell proliferation by downregulating the expression of CDK2, RRM2, and CHEK1, thereby hindering cell cycle progression and regulating the p53 signaling pathway. Notably, the downregulation of these key glioblastoma-related target genes was validated by qPCR. In addition, network pharmacology analysis indicated that several peptide families present in the sea anemone crude venom, including ShK peptides, inhibitor cystine knot (ICK) peptides, and EGF-like peptides, exhibit notable antitumor potential. Combined with AlphaFold2-based structural modeling and molecular docking, these analyses further elucidated the potential molecular mechanisms underlying their interactions with key targets, such as MD-381 with RRM2, MD-322 with CDK2, and MD-429 with CHEK1. Collectively, these findings highlight the therapeutic potential of M. doreensis crude venom and lay a foundation for the subsequent isolation of novel peptides and their further development in glioblastoma treatment.
abstract_zh: 胶质母细胞瘤是一种高度侵袭性的原发性脑肿瘤，预后较差，亟需新的治疗策略。源自多丽海葵（Macrodactyla doreensis）的毒素因其潜在抗癌活性而受到关注。本研究评估了多丽海葵粗毒对两种常用胶质母细胞瘤细胞系（U251和LN229）的抗癌和细胞毒性效应，这些细胞系反映了原发肿瘤的表型。通过CCK-8实验和集落形成实验评估细胞活力和增殖能力，而细胞迁移和侵袭能力则通过划痕愈合实验和Transwell实验检测。Annexin V/PI染色和基于PI的细胞周期分析表明，粗毒显著诱导细胞凋亡并引起S期阻滞。蛋白质组学分析结合GO和KEGG富集分析以及生物信息学方法显示，多丽海葵粗毒通过下调CDK2、RRM2和CHEK1的表达来抑制胶质母细胞瘤细胞增殖，从而阻碍细胞周期进程并调控p53信号通路。值得注意的是，这些关键胶质母细胞瘤相关靶基因的下调已通过qPCR验证。此外，网络药理学分析表明，海葵粗毒中存在的多个肽家族，包括ShK肽、抑制剂胱氨酸结（ICK）肽和EGF样肽，表现出显著的抗肿瘤潜力。结合基于AlphaFold2的结构建模和分子对接，这些分析进一步阐明了它们与关键靶点（如MD-381与RRM2、MD-322与CDK2、MD-429与CHEK1）相互作用的潜在分子机制。总体而言，这些发现凸显了多丽海葵粗毒的治疗潜力，并为后续新型肽的分离及其在胶质母细胞瘤治疗中的进一步开发奠定了基础。
